reason: The reported three-significant-figure outputs, 4.23e24 fissions and 5.56 kg, are correct. However, the required raw results and Lean model replace the problem’s printed constants (1 eV = 1.602e-19 J and N_A = 6.022e23 mol^-1) with higher-precision modern SI values. This contradicts TASK.json’s exact-as-printed measurement policy. Using the printed constants gives raw values TN = 4.2306727821324856e24 and m = 5.559734009599031 kg, not the submitted 4.230206366232802e24 and 5.558991132160095 kg, although both pairs round to the submitted final values.

coverage.evidence: The source-derived 185.20 MeV fission energy, 30-kiloton conversion, energy balance, uniqueness, and 4.23e24 rounding interval are substantively proved. The theorem nevertheless uses TrustedLaw.joulePerMeV = 1.602176634e-13 J rather than the source-sheet value 1.602e-13 J, so its raw expression is not the source-required one.

The 90% mass fraction, 33% fission fraction, inventory balance, uniqueness, and 5.56 kg rounding interval are substantively proved. Its raw expression inherits the wrong MeV conversion and additionally uses N_A = 6.02214076e23 instead of the printed 6.022e23 mol^-1.

unsupported_assumptions: The candidate assumes higher-precision external SI constants supersede the rounded constants stipulated in the original problem’s physical-constants sheet.

The identification of 235.04 u with exactly 235.04 g mol^-1 is modeled as exact. The current SI relation includes the experimentally determined molar-mass constant; the approximation is harmless at three significant figures but is not exact, as explained by the [BIPM SI Brochure](https://www.bipm.org/documents/20126/41483022/SI-Brochure-9.pdf).
